original.target_description: Published Bradley, Mogg, Falla, and Hamilton (1998), single study: forced-choice probe discrimination task with threat-neutral and happy-neutral face pairs, high/low trait anxiety groups, 500 and 1250 msec exposure durations. The supplied description and page locator do not uniquely identify an outcome/contrast/test.

notes: Fresh original-only blind validation. Supplied published article title/authors/year match the assigned reference. Visually inspected rendered PDF pp.7-10 (printed pp.743-746). PDF p.10 is entirely Figure 1, displaying both threat and happy bias scores for both anxiety groups at both exposure durations; it prints no F/t statistic or p value. Surrounding canonical text reports separate omnibus interactions, group effects for each face type, planned between-group contrasts at each duration, and within-group tests against zero. Description "Probe detection task." plus locator "p.10" does not choose among these tests. Accordingly no statistic or p was selected and target_match remains unknown. The available paper is not classified unavailable. Ancillary sample evidence, not promoted into a target-specific n field under the failure-side rule: printed p.743 (PDF p.7), Attentional Task, states "For the ® nal sam ple (n = 38), the mean percentage s of data lost". Rendered page confirms final sample n = 38; canonical-text glyphs and spacing preserved in this quote. Participants section (printed p.741) describes two participant exclusions, poor eyesight and outlying reaction times; Attentional Task describes error-trial removal, RT outlier removal below 250 or above 850 msec, and exclusion of a volunteer with 25% missing data. Canonical text uses spacing artifacts, ® for the fi ligature, and 3 for multiplication signs; rendered p.745 confirms multiplication signs in the ANOVAs, but none was normalized into a quotation. No secondary-source original values used. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
